notes: Things the rewrite may want: (1) Cooper's lakes were mostly clear (44 of 53 "white" water) and held smelt and golden shiner, so they differ from Hot Brook in the ways the paper notes. (2) Cooper's "Red-bellied Sunfish (Lepomis auritus)" is the redbreast sunfish: 19 by gill net and 177 by seine in these lakes, plus 13 hybrids with pumpkinseed (pp. 103, 121), relevant to §3.5.3's "uncommon to rare in lakes". (3) Appendix A's Anasagunticook bass ate 45 % crayfish (see the crayfish claim). (4) The white perch growing season began in the first or second week of July (scale annuli, p. 154).
